checkpoints.name: lint_flags_shadow
checkpoints.description: LintCrux reports `shadow` as an unused signal in the register file — a dead scratch register left in the RTL.

checkpoints.name: lint_flags_unused_addr_bits
checkpoints.description: LintCrux also reports that the low address bits are unused — the decoder only looks at the top nibble.

checkpoints.name: structure_top
checkpoints.description: In NetCrux, mem_ctrl is assembled from the address decoder and the register file.

checkpoints.name: regfile_has_three_real_registers
checkpoints.description: The register file synthesises to exactly three flip-flop banks — ctrl, data0, data1. Not four: the `shadow` register lint flagged has been dead-code-eliminated by synthesis, so it is not in the structure at all. This is the crossing the pack teaches — a lint finding whose resolution is visible in the netlist.

cross_tool_deep_links.name: shadow_lint_to_structure
cross_tool_deep_links.source_action: open the UNUSEDSIGNAL finding on `shadow` and cross-probe to the structure
cross_tool_deep_links.expected_target_state: the regfile module is shown, and `shadow` is absent from its synthesised cells — confirming the unused register was dropped, so the finding is safe to resolve by deleting it
